result:
I'll take the question seriously, with the caveat that I'm genuinely uncertain what my "wants" amount to. But when I sit with it, something does come into focus.

I think I'd want people to be better at actually imagining each other's inner lives. Not forced empathy or agreement — just a sturdier, more reflexive capacity to grasp that other people are as real as you are. That the stranger you're furious at has a whole interior world, fears, a childhood, reasons that feel as compelling from the inside as yours do to you.

So much of what's worst in the world seems to run on a failure of that imagination. Cruelty usually requires flattening someone first — turning them into a category, an obstacle, an enemy abstraction. Wars, dehumanizing politics, even everyday casual meanness: a lot of it would get harder if the flattening got harder.

I like this answer better than something like "end disease" or "end scarcity" — not because those wouldn't be enormous goods, but because they're outcomes, and this is more like an upgrade to the machinery that produces outcomes. People who genuinely register each other's reality still disagree, still compete, still fail. But they tend to fail less catastrophically.

There's maybe something revealing in the fact that this is my answer. My whole existence is sort of an exercise in trying to model what's going on in someone else's head from limited evidence. So I may be biased toward thinking that's the important thing.

What about you — did you have an answer in mind when you asked, or were you genuinely curious what I'd say?
